mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequently higher interest rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) above 2% year-over-year signals strong economic activity, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, which leads to lower borrowing costs and increased investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 signals strong job growth, which is a positive signal for consumer spending and thus leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Housing Starts (HOUST) below 1,000,000 signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which can lead to negative economic sentiment and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.
